epic.intent: Replace native Bannerlord player combat with a controller-first action system inspired by Dragon's Dogma 2: button-driven light/heavy combos, blocking, dodging, freely arranged unlocked LT abilities, distinct Foot/Mounted loadouts, and new combat menus/HUD. Reuse existing Bannerlord weapons and practical native assets, preserve real weapon restrictions, and adapt AI defenses/reactions only. Controller ergonomics and full gamepad navigation are central acceptance requirements. User confirmed design/epic planning only on 2026-10-09; this saved backlog is a future implementation plan, not implemented or runtime-verified combat. Detailed design proposals and technical proof requirements are in the rationale. Other modders must be able to add independently packaged abilities with their own animations through a documented public authoring kit, without editing or recompiling the combat framework. Common abilities are declarative; advanced effects use an optional versioned extension API. This is a required outcome, with independent-author acceptance.

successCriteria.text: Controller-only play reaches every new menu and essential combat/order/mount action without mouse-direction attacks, lost focus, unassigned actions or leaked LT chords; remapping, camera/aim assistance, accessibility and hotplug are verified.

The player performs light/heavy/mixed/charged melee chains, facing-based block and collision-safe dodge with readable commitment, stamina, reliable cancellation and one authoritative native hit pipeline.

Players freely choose and arrange unlocked skills in four LT slots for Foot and four separately saved Mounted slots, with compatible alternatives, clear restrictions, safe page transitions and shared resource/cooldown rules.

All native player weapon usages in the pinned installed roster have tested behavior, including one-hand/shield, two-hand, polearm, bow, crossbow, throwing, unarmed and present exceptional usages; ammo/reload/mounted restrictions remain correct.

Loadout, preset, library, controls/accessibility, training and HUD flows work on controller and keyboard/mouse, persist per hero/user as appropriate and safely recover from old or missing definitions.

Native AI defenses/reactions and required mission contexts remain functional, including enabled War Sails integration; no full AI player-skill rewrite or dependency on procedural world generation is introduced.

A version-pinned clean package has passing capability probes, automated invariants and in-game controller/mission/save/performance evidence; required unsupported or untested behavior is reported as failed/blocked, never complete.

An independent modder uses only the published kit/docs to create a separate ability module with original custom foot and mounted animations, validates/packages it without changing the framework, and sees it work in controller loadouts, native-hit gameplay and saves. Public SDK/examples, pack coexistence/version diagnostics and missing-pack recovery pass.

epic.title: Controller-first Bannerlord combat overhaul inspired by Dragon's Dogma 2

bundle.rationale:
# Status and confirmed scope

This is the next implementation epic, planned on 2026-10-09. No combat mod has been implemented, compiled, installed or played in this planning task. The repository contains planner metadata, not an existing combat codebase. “Teardown” therefore means replacing the native player combat interaction through a new mod, after inventorying the installed game's behavior; it does not mean deleting nonexistent source or modifying official game files. Every proposed source path below is a future implementation artifact. Documentation/API existence is not runtime proof.

The user explicitly requested Dragon's Dogma 2 as the inspiration, light and heavy combos, blocking, dodging, customizable LT abilities, a distinct mounted skillset, existing Bannerlord weapon options, new menus, and a ground-up controller-friendly design. The user clarified: write the epic/design first; players freely choose and arrange unlocked skills, not edit ability effects; overhaul player combat and adapt AI defenses/reactions, without giving the army the full player ability system.

Controller usability is a release requirement, not a final keybinding pass. A controller user must navigate every new menu, select skills, fight in melee and at range, issue troop orders, mount/dismount and resume after death or a device change without reaching for a mouse. Keyboard/mouse must remain a supported alternate input path through the same actions. The proposal targets PC single-player campaign and combat missions; multiplayer replication, a console release and redesigning unrelated kingdom/trade interfaces are not added to this epic. The affected native mission, equipment, pause and order flows must still work from a controller.

The existing FWGC++/War Sails world-generation epic remains unchanged. Combat has no dependency on its generator or world renderer. Support standard campaigns first and compatible generated-world missions through ordinary mission contracts. War Sails integration is required when that module is installed/enabled, including ship-deck combat and contextual controls. A missing DLC is recorded as unavailable for that integration scenario, never as proof it passed.

The following concrete control scheme, skill catalog and balance values are DESIGN PROPOSALS to implement and tune, not claims that DD2 has identical controls. Capcom's manual describes vocation-dependent skills/guard/evade. This mod deliberately brings light/heavy, guard and dodge intents into one Bannerlord player framework, constrained by the equipped weapon. It does not import DD2 code, names, animations, music, vocations or assets. No new magic, dual-wield system, monster climbing, pawn system or weapon category is needed.

# Player experience and input grammar

Default Xbox-layout labels (platform-equivalent glyphs follow the actual device): left stick moves/steers, right stick looks/aims, RB performs light melee, RT performs heavy melee (tap normal heavy, hold/release charged heavy where supported), LB guards, B dodges, A jumps, X interacts, Y taps to cycle equipped weapons or holds for equipment selection. L3 toggles sprint/gallop; R3 toggles optional target focus. D-pad Up toggles troop-command overlay; remaining native stance/weapon-use/utility controls are reconciled in the input audit and exposed through a fully controller-navigable contextual selector rather than dropped. Start opens pause with Combat Arts and Combat Settings entries. No combat action requires mouse-direction selection or rapid right-stick flicks to choose attack direction.

LT is an ability modifier. LT+A/B/X/Y maps to four assignable slots on the active Foot or Mounted page. Four slots per page is this design's proposed default. A chord consumes its face button until release: LT+B never also dodges, LT+A never jumps, LT+X never interacts and LT+Y never switches weapons. Instant skills fire once on chord-down. Aimed skills enter an armed targeting state, release the thumb to the right stick, then use RT to confirm and B to cancel; releasing LT alone does not accidentally fire. Releasing/canceling consumes all held action buttons until re-armed. Invalid skills show a short reason, never silently cast something else.

Priority: modal UI > troop orders > interaction/weapon selector > armed skill targeting > LT skill layer > ordinary combat. A single arbiter owns actions; no native and mod path both execute one press. Input sampled before a mode change cannot be replayed into the new mode. Pause, focus loss, controller disconnect, knockout, player-agent replacement, mount changes and equipment transitions clear buffered actions and neutralize holds; a fresh press is required. Disconnect pauses when the mission permits; otherwise suppresses new player actions and reports connection loss without freezing the battle simulation globally. Remapped actions and toggle/hold settings must use the same arbiter.

Troop-command overlay: D-pad Up opens/closes it; right stick selects a command, LB/RB select eligible formations/groups, RT confirms, B cancels. Left stick continues movement where native behavior permits, with camera context clearly indicated. Formation selection, facing, placement, charge/follow/hold and available naval/siege orders must remain reachable; the audit determines actual native command coverage. UI/command inputs must not become attacks. Targeting input resumes from the current camera orientation without snapping on close.

Ranged contexts retain real native ammo, draw, reload and projectile behavior. RT holds/toggles precision aim; RB draws/releases a bow, fires a loaded crossbow or starts its valid reload, or primes/releases a throwing weapon according to the weapon's state. Light/heavy labels become family-specific Quick/Power or Fire/Aim prompts; do not fake a three-shot crossbow combo or melee-style heavy when it bypasses loading. The same LB/B/LT defensive/skill grammar applies, with guard available only when equipment supports it. Aim settings include sensitivity, inversion, inner/outer deadzones, response curve, aim-assist strength, controller glyphs and vibration. Never require trigger strength beyond an adjustable digital threshold.

Mounted movement stays native steering/turn radius/speed. RB/RT select appropriate side/attack arcs with camera-relative intent and compatible usage; LB guards if the equipped configuration permits. B performs a bounded mounted evasive maneuver (brief lateral steer/deceleration) rather than a foot roll, teleport or arbitrary horse invulnerability. A uses the native mount jump where available. Hold X to mount/dismount when the native prompt permits; distinguish tap interactions and dangerous dismounts. Couch/brace/alternate weapon use remains a named contextual action with native speed and usage restrictions. LT automatically changes to the Mounted page after authoritative mount confirmation, and back only after confirmed dismount. UI clearly names the active page.

# Combat rules and feel

Use one deterministic action state machine: idle/move, windup, active, recovery, guarding, dodging, aiming/reloading, ability, stagger, mount transition, disabled. Death/knockout/mission removal dominates all other states. Animation progress and a mission simulation clock drive gameplay windows; never count render frames. A bounded one-action buffer accepts a proposed 150 ms early input; new valid intent replaces the previous pending intent. Expired, incompatible or transition-crossing inputs are discarded with diagnostic reasons. Pause freezes windows; low/high frame rates do not change timings.

Melee profiles propose L1-L2-L3 and H1-H2 chains, plus explicitly authored L-L-H finishers and H-L followups where animation/weapon usage support them. Heavy attacks emphasize commitment, reach/stagger or guard pressure; lights emphasize responsive pressure. Holding a supported heavy charges up to a capped maximum, releases on button-up, and has a readable cue. Basic attacks function without lock-on; soft aim bias may help a target inside a forward cone but cannot rotate through walls or retarget mid-active swing. Startup can accept a defensive cancel only in tagged windows, active frames commit, recovery has a tagged cancel window. Stagger/death/weapon changes reset chains. Default timing, damage and charge values are data, measured and tuned against the pinned animation set.

One player stamina pool (proposed 100 units) covers attacks, dodge, guard impacts and abilities. Example starting values: light 5, heavy 15, dodge 20, ability 15-35, regeneration 20/s after 0.75 s idle recovery; these are initial tuning hypotheses, not observed balance. Never spend below zero. One action reserves costs at acceptance and commits at the declared effect frame. Cancellation before commitment refunds the unspent reservation; after commitment no refund. Cooldown starts at the same declared commitment point. Native ammunition is consumed by the authoritative projectile pipeline exactly once. Guard drains on impacts; guard break/stagger has a finite recovery and a resistance window to prevent infinite stun locks. Low stamina disables unaffordable actions with feedback; it must not trap the player in a state with no exit.

LB is facing-based guard, with shield coverage or a weapon parry arc resolved from actual equipment. Controller assistance chooses a defensible direction inside that arc; no 360-degree block or mouse-direction requirement. Shield durability, armor, damage type, reach, perks and native blockable/unblockable rules remain meaningful. Weapons that cannot guard show that reason; no invisible shield for a bow or bare hands. A short initial timed-guard window is a proposed skill expression bonus, not mandatory perfect parry for ordinary defense. Dodge is a ground-constrained step/roll with authored displacement, stamina cost and recovery. Physical evasion is required. An explicit configurable invulnerability window is a proposed optional enhancement only if the runtime probe proves reliable filtering; otherwise use the documented physical-evasion-only profile and show that disposition, without blocking dodge or pretending immunity exists. Obstacles, slopes, falls, ladders and ship decks constrain displacement. No collision-through-wall fallback counts as success.

Native hit/collision owns contacts, armor, shields, damage attribution, XP, kill feeds, friendly-fire policy and projectile physics. The mod adds action identity/windows and controlled modifiers around one authoritative resolution path. A hit ledger keyed by action instance/target/hit segment prevents duplicate damage while preserving authored cleaves and multi-strikes. Native reach/speed/equipment flags still apply. Never combine native damage plus a second synthetic damage event. Hit-stop, shake, rumble and effects are local feedback; never pause the whole battle for one player's impact. Shake/flash/vibration are adjustable or disabled.

# Native weapon coverage

Resolve the active WeaponComponentData/usage, not just item display name or broad item type. Build a manifest from installed modules and all supported native player-equippable usages. Crafted hybrids, swapped usage, shield loss, pickup/drop, broken equipment and temporary tournament gear recompute the profile. Every manifest entry has supported behavior or an explicit reason for a native contextual fallback. A niche unsupported animation cannot silently erase a requested core family.

- One-handed swords, axes and maces: distinct short light chain, committed heavy chain, native reach/damage identity; shield and no-shield variants; dagger where the installed roster offers it. No assumed sword stab on an axe/mace.
- Two-handed swords, axes and blunt weapons: slower light chain, charged heavy/cleave where supported, stamina/recovery exposure, weapon guard; preserve the actual weapon's flags and simultaneous-hit behavior.
- Polearms: spear/pike thrust profiles, cutting polearm swings only on permitted usages, one/two-handed/shield variants, couched mounted lances and on-foot bracing only when native conditions permit. Long confined-space collisions matter.
- Bows: draw/release cadence, aim, charged precision and real ammo; no animation-only instant projectile. Crossbows: loaded/unloaded/reloading states, aimed shot and explicit mounted reload restrictions.
- Throwing knives/axes/javelins: native stock count, hold/release aim, compatible melee alternate usage; no infinite ammunition or invented rapid-throw animation.
- Shields: directional coverage, block reaction, native durability and compatible offense; shield strike is only enabled after its contact/reaction probe passes.
- Unarmed and exceptional installed weapons: safe light/heavy/defense disposition using available actions. Current API enums alone do not prove sling/firearm/artillery inventory content. Inspect the actual roster; implement sling handling when present, and keep siege engines/other non-player-equippable tools in native interaction context. No invention of a new firearm/sling system to fill an enum.

# Abilities, loadouts and progression

Each hero has Foot[4] and Mounted[4], independent selections and slot ordering. Players may put any unlocked compatible ability into any slot; no vocation lock, fixed skill package or mandatory class preset. Duplicate IDs within one page are rejected; the same shared ability across pages is allowed and shares its cooldown. A skill incompatible with the currently wielded weapon remains visible and disabled with the exact requirement. The player can select another preset or weapon; the system never silently discards a choice or auto-equips gear. Presets may be named/copied/reset and are snapshots of the two pages, not extra simultaneous pages. Editing happens from a safe campaign or paused mission menu; live action/casting is canceled before entry, and reopening/equipping cannot replenish stamina or cooldowns.

AbilityDefinition v1 includes stable ID, localization keys, foot/mounted eligibility, weapon/usage/shield predicates, native skill unlock, cost, cooldown group, target mode, action/movement recipe, commit point, interruption/refund policy, effect/hit windows and presentation. Ordinary ability packs compose a bounded validated recipe vocabulary without code. Registered third-party effect providers may extend that vocabulary through the versioned public SDK while retaining the same action/resource/collision contracts. No arbitrary data-file script execution or in-game ability-effect editor is required. The required modder-facing framework section below defines discovery, custom animation authoring and public tooling. Reject duplicate IDs, impossible usage, invalid timings, unbounded displacement/effect values and missing localization/assets with precise diagnostics before mission activation.

Proposed initial catalog (original working names, all subject to native action probes): shared Quick Recovery (vulnerable stamina-recovery action, no health heal) and Guard Focus (temporary guard efficiency, requires guard-capable equipment); Foot utility Evasive Step; one-hand Driving Strike and Countercut; shield Shield Check; two-hand Sweeping Blow and Crushing Blow; spear Advancing Thrust and Braced Counter; cutting polearm Reaping Cut; bow Power Shot and Steady Draw; crossbow Braced Shot and Reload Drill; throwing Focused Throw and Running Throw. Common loadouts draw four slots and meaningful alternatives from the named eligibility matrix; exceptional usages retain explicit restrictions. For common foot weapons, where shared skills lack an eligible ranged defense, supply ranged-compatible Focused Footwork rather than fake guard. Evasive Step/Focused Footwork are reposition actions, not projectile generation. Skills retain ammo/animation restrictions; Reload Drill modestly changes a verified reload window, never bypasses a no-mounted-reload restriction.

Mounted catalog: Mounted Quick Recovery (shares recovery cooldown family), Riding Guard (guard-compatible), Evasive Rein (bounded native steering/deceleration), Passing Cut (one-hand/cutting weapon), Heavy Pass (compatible two-hand), Lance Drive (couch-eligible), Spear Jab (compatible thrust), Saddle Shot (bow), Steady Saddle (compatible bow/crossbow/throwing aim), Mounted Throw (throwing), and Loaded Bolt (only a loaded crossbow whose usage permits firing from horseback). Family-incompatible abilities remain disabled. No foot-only skill leaks into the mounted page; common skill identity and shared groups prevent mount/dismount/reset exploits. The named mounted catalog also includes Measured Pace: a vulnerable controlled deceleration and rider stamina recovery action that shares the Quick Recovery cooldown group. Common mounted loadouts have choices beyond four slots; exceptional usages retain explicit restrictions rather than receiving fabricated actions to meet a number.

Progression uses existing Bannerlord weapon/athletics/riding skills. Initial profile proposal: foundation movement/recovery and family starter skills available immediately, advanced abilities unlock at data-defined relevant skill thresholds (initial tiers 25/75/125, calibrated by balance ticket); no separate skill currency or forced respec. Unlocking a skill does not auto-equip it. Menus show required stat, current stat and unlock reason. Existing campaigns are evaluated from current hero skills; free preset/slot editing never resets progression. Temporary gear restricts use but does not delete learned skills.

# Menus, HUD and accessibility

Combat Arts entry is reachable from campaign character/pause and the supported mission pause flow. Screen 1 Loadouts has Foot/Mounted tabs, four large slot cards, current weapon context, preview of requirements, named presets, clear/set/swap/reset, Apply/Cancel and unsaved-change handling. Screen 2 Ability Library has compatible/all/locked filters, family and role categories, current slot indication, effect/cost/cooldown/weapon/mount/unlock descriptions, and replace-slot confirmation. Screen 3 Controls and Accessibility provides remapping, conflict resolution, hold/toggle options, deadzones, sensitivities, aim assist, glyph preference, rumble, shake/flash and readable HUD sizing. The Training entry launches or enters a controlled native-compatible arena/tutorial for practice without consuming campaign inventory or changing campaign outcomes; exit restores the original state. Native menu lifecycle must be proven before promising a new mission launcher.

Controller focus never disappears. A confirms, B backs/cancels, shoulder buttons change tabs, D-pad/stick move focus, long lists scroll selected entries into view; prompts reflect the current remap/device. Mouse interaction is optional, not required to recover focus. Hotplug and switching devices preserve selection without double activation. Focus/contrast/text/icon distinguish locked, unavailable, empty and cooling-down states without color alone. No mouse hover-only explanation or drag-only slot rearrangement. Check common aspect ratios/UI scaling and long/localized strings.

HUD shows stamina/guard state, light/heavy/charge/combo cues, reticle/focus target and active Foot/Mounted badge. LT expands a four-slot diamond with actual bindings, name, cost, cooldown and invalid reason; release collapses it. Armed targeting shows confirm/cancel and a clear target validity indicator. Never overload the scene with full skill prose. Essential health, ammo, mount, troop-order and objective information remains readable. All new visible strings use localization keys.

# Technical boundaries, probes and persistence

Proposed module split: src/MNBL.Combat.Core (pure state/input/definitions/loadout logic), src/MNBL.Combat (version-specific Bannerlord host and mission adapters), src/MNBL.Combat.UI (Gauntlet views/view-models), ModuleData/Combat (versioned profiles/abilities/localization), tests/Combat.Core and tests/Combat.Runtime (fixtures/scenarios), evidence/combat (observations). Share interfaces deliberately; one writer owns a file. Reuse established Doctor/build/package helpers if the other epic implements them first; do not overwrite them or add an artificial dependency on world generation. A future epic branch should use codex/ unless the user specifies another name; planning does not create/checkout a branch.

First inventory installed game/module versions, assembly hashes, target framework, Modding Kit availability and existing combat mods. Compile against the installed build, not an arbitrary API documentation version. Audit baseline input, combat animations, active weapon usages, native mission paths, troop orders, hit/block callbacks and player ownership. Required probes separately establish exclusive input routing; actual player action/animation changes and contact resolution; bounded foot/mounted movement and camera control; UI focus/pause integration and supported save boundaries. Compile/API reflection alone cannot pass a runtime probe. Missing native capability blocks dependent features and records an exact reproduction; it never turns the request into a vanilla-keybinding-only release. Prefer public supported adapters; any justified patch must be version-scoped, reversible, narrowly targeted and conflict-detected, with third-party provenance recorded.

Core contracts: InputIntent v1 carries sequence, source device, context epoch, phase and simulation timestamp; CombatAction v1 carries actor/action IDs, weapon usage, windup/active/recovery, legal next/cancel transitions and resource commitment; CombatEvent v1 records one authoritative result; WeaponProfile v1 resolves native usage and context restrictions; AbilityDefinition v1 is above; CharacterCombatSave v1 contains schema version, stable hero/preset/skill IDs, Foot/Mounted pages, unlock policy version and supported resource/cooldown state. Settings v1 stores user-wide control/accessibility preferences separately. Runtime actor pointers, action handles and absolute process clocks never enter a save.

Timers advance on the appropriate game simulation clock and freeze with pause. Cooldowns are shared by declared group across skill pages/presets/weapons; only remaining durations are serialized at supported save boundaries and restored relative to the new clock. Combat transient state never survives a mission/reload. Do not claim Bannerlord supports arbitrary mid-battle saves. Mission exit/capture/death policies define retained remaining cooldowns and stamina recovery during normal campaign simulation; transitions cannot be spammed for a free refill. Original save data is retained on unknown IDs/schema incompatibility; show a repair report and allow reselection, never overwrite the user's known-good save with an empty loadout. Loading two different heroes/campaigns must not share mutable presets or resources. Disabling the mod uses a documented supported recovery path, with backups and no promise of unconditional mid-campaign removal until tested.

AI keeps native movement/attack/formation decision-making. Adapt guard direction, reaction windows, hit/stagger recognition and difficulty-bounded perception so native agents respond to the player's new actions. They must not read future buffered input or block unseen attacks instantaneously. No per-frame ability simulation for every soldier. Mission compatibility covers field battles, sieges, hideouts, tournaments/practice, settlement fights, ladders, siege engines, spectating, death, retreat, surrender/capture and War Sails ship-deck/boarding contexts when enabled. Cinematics, conversations and other noncombat controls keep their native owner. Unsupported contexts display deliberate behavior; required combat contexts cannot be quietly excluded.

# Verification and delivery contract

One execution sprint contains parallel work branches, with one final integrated acceptance/human handoff. Logical phases are environment/probes, combat foundation, weapon/ability content, mounted+menus, compatibility/QA/package. They are not intermediate product approval gates. Capability failures stop only dependent tickets; independent core/data/UI work can continue using explicit fixtures. Planning ends with the saved backlog epic and no started execution run.

Unit/contract checks cover timing across 30/60/120 Hz stepping, input precedence/chord leakage, transition epochs, invalid definitions, reservation/refund/commit, duplicate hit prevention, unlock boundaries, loadout validation/migration and timer persistence. Runtime evidence must additionally show animation/contact/AI/camera/UI behavior; unit tests cannot establish feel or engine support.

Final controller-only scenario starts a known supported campaign/package, opens all new menus, remaps a conflicting action and repairs it, assigns/swaps/clears and saves both pages, and plays the tutorial. Fight a native AI group with each supported weapon family: light and heavy chains, charged attack, guard/timed guard, dodge under attack, instant and aimed LT skills, ranged ammo/reload limits, no stamina/cooldown duplication. Issue formation orders mid-fight, change weapons, pick up/drop gear, lose a shield, mount/dismount repeatedly during buffered/held input, kill/lose a mount and confirm safe page changes. Exercise mounted melee/ranged skill restrictions and native jump/steering/couch rules. Run the required mission-context matrix and ship-deck cases when enabled. Disconnect/reconnect and switch input devices; every required action/menu remains reachable without a mouse. Save at actual supported boundaries, cold-restart, reload two campaigns/heroes and verify page/preset/unlock/resource separation and missing-definition repair on copies. Check mod-disabled baseline and package installation without developer paths.

Record exact game/modules/build/commit/config/hardware/controller identities, action logs, videos/screenshots of required behavior, timings and pass/fail/blocked/not-run per criterion. Baseline and modded battle runs use the same scenario/agent count/settings. Provisional performance targets are <=10% p95 and <=15% p99 mission frame time regression. The implementer derives actual acceptance thresholds from the recorded baseline/hardware/workload before optimization; these example percentages are not an invented universal release blocker. No growing allocations/subscriptions across ten mission transitions and no missed/duplicate actions in scripted replay are required. Material controller/gameplay degradation must be resolved and reported. Record actual numbers and selected battle size; do not invent a hardware-independent FPS guarantee. Input acceptance should occur within one simulation update for an idle valid press; authored animation windup is measured separately. Playtest fixes focus on responsiveness, readable commitment and controller comfort; no claim of DD2 quality from a green build alone.

Every work ticket has its own observable criteria and a covering final acceptance criterion. Required runtime gaps remain failed/blocked; no stubs or “implemented but untested” completion. The final evidence index links each requirement to current component and integrated evidence; stale evidence is rerun only when affected. Package only owned source/data/assets with required notices, never native game binaries. Deliver build/install/remove/recovery instructions and a concise remaining-risk list grounded in observed behavior.


# Catalog behavior and implementation precision

Skill names in the proposal denote the following bounded behavior. Every production definition additionally receives verified native action IDs, simulation-time windows, numeric tuning and an eligibility fixture in A02/A03/M02. Exact costs/cooldowns are tuning data; no skill may invent a projectile, bypass guard restrictions, grant healing, teleport, or reset shared resources.

- Quick Recovery: stationary vulnerable rider/foot recovery after a commitment delay, no HP healing; interrupt before commitment gives no gain. Mounted Quick Recovery uses the same recovery group. Measured Pace: mounted-only controlled deceleration plus a smaller recovery benefit, same group, no forced horse turn.
- Guard Focus / Riding Guard: temporarily reduce impact stamina cost while a valid native weapon/shield guard is actually held; no defense outside the normal arc. Ends on equipment/context invalidation.
- Evasive Step: foot directional physical evasion with a longer committed recovery than ordinary dodge. Focused Footwork: brief reduced movement penalty while preparing/aiming a valid foot weapon, with melee and ranged eligibility explicitly checked against native preparation states, no increased projectile speed or free immunity. Evasive Rein: short native-bounded mounted steer/deceleration under player direction, never foot-roll displacement. These count as distinct utility choices, not hidden duplicate cooldown charges.
- Driving Strike: one-handed short advancing native strike, commits on attack activation, stops at collision. Countercut: one-hand response available during a finite window after a real successful guard; no hit guarantees. Shield Check: short verified shield contact and limited stagger only for an equipped intact shield and supported action.
- Sweeping Blow: supported two-hand broad attack with native collision/cleave limits. Crushing Blow: slower committed heavy with bounded guard-pressure/stagger modifier; never unconditional unblockable damage.
- Advancing Thrust: thrust-capable spear/pike step and stab with physical reach. Braced Counter: on-foot brace-capable usage only, stationary preparation and real incoming contact. Reaping Cut: cutting-polearm swing only, not available to a thrust-only spear.
- Power Shot: bow-only charged/aimed release with extra preparation and one native arrow. Steady Draw: temporary aim stability during a valid native draw, ending on incompatible action. Braced Shot: loaded crossbow precise shot after stationary preparation. Reload Drill: bounded reload timing adjustment on a reload-capable usage, preserving the prohibition on horseback reload where present.
- Focused Throw: one deliberately aimed/committed native throw. Running Throw: one native throw with a bounded preparation movement penalty reduction. Both require actual stock and obey native aiming arcs; no homing or free follow-up projectile.
- Passing Cut / Heavy Pass: one-handed or supported two-hand side strike during a ride, bounded target/facing adjustment, no automatic horse steering. Lance Drive: enhanced commitment to a native-valid couched pass with the actual speed/usage restriction. Spear Jab: native-mounted thrust on a compatible usage.
- Saddle Shot: bow-only prepared native shot while riding, one arrow. Steady Saddle: temporary native aim stability for a compatible bow/crossbow/throwing usage, including mounted throwing; it requires the native aiming state and does not change projectile guidance. Mounted Throw: one compatible native thrown release. Loaded Bolt: compatible loaded crossbow shot, never a reload bypass. Native bow/crossbow/throwing limitations remain visible in the library.

The provisional core input contract and schemas belong to D01/D02. Native roster evidence comes from F02. W01 builds the resolver/index and representative schema fixtures; W02-W06 author production family profiles; W07 closes the full manifest after those profiles exist. UI models can consume immutable events/contracts without controlling combat; M01 proves a page-change event, U04 proves its rendered badge. A01 depends on L01 for real unlock eligibility. A03 depends on A02 for shared foot utility. Mounted profile implementation waits for native-compatible one-hand/two-hand/polearm profiles, and AI validation waits for the player catalog it must recognize. Q03 reruns affected checks after tuning so final acceptance never reuses stale feel/timing evidence.

# Primary research and limits

Research was read on 2026-10-09. The official API index exposes 1.4.8, while accessible runtime pages below are explicitly 1.4.7; neither has been established as the installed target. These are candidate contracts to investigate, not code verified against the user's game. [Official API versions](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/).

- Active usage, rather than an item name, exposes the relevant equipped behavior. Resolve CurrentUsageItem/CurrentUsageIndex and the weapon's data/flags. Native mount/shield/reload predicates must be carried into ability validation. [MissionWeapon](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.7/struct_tale_worlds_1_1_mount_and_blade_1_1_mission_weapon.html), [WeaponComponentData](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.8/class_tale_worlds_1_1_core_1_1_weapon_component_data.html), [Item usage flags](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.8/class_tale_worlds_1_1_core_1_1_item_object.html), [MBItem usage lookup](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.7/class_tale_worlds_1_1_mount_and_blade_1_1_m_b_item.html).
- The documented taxonomy includes native melee/ranged classes plus entries that need not be player inventory items; 1.4.8 also exposes sling entries. Installed roster discovery determines scope. [Weapon classes and flags](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.8/namespace_tale_worlds_1_1_core.html).
- Input contexts expose press/down/release, axes/sticks and connection queries; game-key contexts provide configurable keys. Exclusive native suppression and safe chords still require P01. # Required modder-facing ability framework (user clarification, 2026-10-09)

Adding abilities must be easy for other modders, including their own animations. This is a mandatory outcome of the combat epic, not a future stretch goal. The framework ships both player-facing combat and a public ability-authoring kit. This clarification expands third-party authoring; it does not change the earlier decision that players select and arrange authored skills rather than edit ability effects in an in-game editor.

## Author journey and supported extension levels

The ordinary path is: create a separate Bannerlord module from the supplied template; add one ability definition; choose a native animation or import an original compatible animation using the documented native tools; bind animation phases and effect windows; supply optional icons/audio/VFX/localized text; validate; package; enable the module alongside the combat framework and launch the game. An ability made from existing action/effect primitives requires no C# build, core source checkout, fork, core JSON edit, new UI screen, or manual per-skill registration in the combat mod. Asset import/baking may still require Bannerlord's native authoring tools; “easy” must not falsely imply raw animation files can be dropped directly into a running game. The toolkit lists exact prerequisites, commands, generated paths and restart requirements and reports what the author needs to fix.

Declarative definitions compose supported target modes, weapon/mount predicates, resource/cooldown groups, unlock requirements, movement/action phases, animation bindings, native-hit modifiers and presentation. Defaults are useful: the template needs only identity/display text, context/equipment eligibility and an action/animation recipe; optional fields get documented defaults, with generated examples showing how to override them. Controller buttons are never hardcoded in an ability pack. Packs expose skill identity and targeting semantics; the player chooses LT slots and the framework renders remapped glyphs.

For genuinely new mechanics, provide an optional versioned C# SDK with public effect/provider interfaces and a working example. A separate ordinary Bannerlord code module registers an effect factory against that API. The framework supplies actor/context/target checks, action phases, cancellation, resource commitment, shared cooldowns, native-hit ownership and disposal contracts. Extensions receive a documented context and issue supported commands instead of needing private reflection, a core fork or duplicate damage hooks. Common declarative skills never require this route. A managed provider callback exception before or after commitment follows the same defined cancel/refund rules and always releases framework-owned temporary effects; log the pack/skill/phase and reject further activation until a safe recovery boundary. Do not promise recovery from arbitrary native crashes. The SDK is an extensibility API, not a security sandbox: arbitrary native code mods retain normal Bannerlord code-mod risks and must not be presented as isolated untrusted scripts.

## Pack contract and discovery

Proposed public contracts: AbilityPackManifest v1, AbilityDefinition v1, AnimationBinding v1, EffectProvider API v1 and an authoring SDK compatibility version separate from gameplay balance. A pack is an enabled native module with its own metadata, assets and namespaced stable pack/ability/effect IDs (for example author.pack/ability-name). Native asset/action names use a generated prefix legal for the engine, not an assumption that the stable-ID separator is accepted by native XML. All resource references are pack-relative or explicitly qualified external dependencies. Resolve against enabled modules and their declared dependency/load order, never a scan that silently loads disabled packs.

Manifest fields include pack ID/version, supported framework API/game-build range, required/optional pack dependencies and versions, ability definition paths, native module/resource/action bindings, localization/icon/audio/VFX roots, and optional effect-provider registration. Use one documented module-relative content location and manifest; avoid per-pack core configuration. First-party abilities load through the same registry/contracts as external packs, without a privileged hardcoded allowlist or built-in-only UI path. The public effect registry is allowlisted by actual registered provider IDs, not a closed list requiring core edits whenever an author adds an effect.

Discovery is deterministic. Distinct namespaces may reuse a local ability name; duplicate fully qualified IDs and dependency cycles are diagnosed, never silently last-wins. No implicit overrides of another pack: any supported replacement must be explicitly declared, opt-in and version-checked. Missing/unsupported framework versions, missing dependencies, invalid recipes, broken asset bindings and unknown effect types report module/ability/file/field and a suggested correction. Declarative/provider-registration failures quarantine only the affected optional pack and dependents before activation; the base catalog remains usable. A required built-in pack failure visibly prevents framework activation through the established native fallback policy. Native asset load failures may occur before managed registration: preflight checks and the tested module-loading procedure must address those separately; do not promise that all malformed binary assets can be safely quarantined at runtime. Bound data and recipe validation as already required by D02/A01.

Loading/unloading custom native resources may require a full game restart. The release workflow guarantees correct startup discovery and restart-based iteration; live import/hot reload is not required and must not be claimed until proven. List loaded pack versions, rejected packs and restart-needed state in a compact diagnostics view available from Combat Settings, with useful author-facing logs. Player screens continue showing gameplay requirements, not internal stack traces.

## Custom animation authoring and runtime proof

Provide a documented template/export/import procedure for the chosen installed Bannerlord version: compatible skeleton/rig and rider/mount context, authored clip/resource naming, resource registration, native action-set/type mapping, blend/priority/speed, root-motion policy and windup/contact/recovery bindings. Offer validation against the pinned native action categories. Imported clips are not arbitrary new engine combat semantics. Framework markers use the action-phase contract mapped to verified native progress/events; do not assume undocumented animation-notify injection is supported.

The official animation guide describes resource animations, action_sets.xml and action_types.xml, engine-recognized action categories and displacement flags. It supports candidate authoring paths, not proof that a custom clip produces correct weapon contacts or behaves on a rider. [TaleWorlds animation authoring](https://moddocs.bannerlord.com/asset-management/asset-types/animations/). Agent action channels are another candidate surface requiring installed-version verification. [Agent API candidate](https://apidoc.bannerlord.com/v/1.4.7/class_tale_worlds_1_1_mount_and_blade_1_1_agent.html).

EX02 must prove a separate module with original custom foot and mounted-rider animations, using an existing compatible weapon and skeleton. Verify startup resource discovery with two packs enabled, load-order/dependency resolution, phase alignment, native collision, exactly one hit/XP attribution, block/parry/AI reactions and safe interruption/recovery. Root motion must respect collision and native mount steering; a static cosmetic emote does not satisfy a custom combat animation. If replacing/registering a required action from a separate module needs supported build-time resource generation, the authoring tool performs it in the add-on's outputs with namespace/conflict checks. Editing the framework or official module files is not an acceptable author workflow. Unsupported engine categories are clearly reported; the shipped example must demonstrate at least one valid custom attack for each requested foot/mounted context rather than leave this requirement hypothetical.

## Automatic player integration and compatibility

Valid external abilities automatically enter the library, unlock evaluation, Foot/Mounted slot selection, presets, targeting, controller HUD and persistence through the public descriptor/registry. No author-created Gauntlet screen or special keybind is required. Custom icons, localization, audio and VFX use the same lifecycle/presentation service, with documented defaults when omitted and clear author diagnostics for invalid required references. External skills obey existing weapon/ammo/mount constraints and the same cost/cancel/cooldown/native-hit rules. A new effect is not permission to duplicate damage or bypass these contracts.

Persist fully qualified skill IDs and relevant definition/provider schema versions. When a pack is disabled/missing/incompatible, preserve its selections and original save payload as unavailable entries with a readable reason; do not silently replace skills or erase the choices. Reinstalling a compatible pack restores availability after normal validation. Explicit author-provided ID aliases/migrations handle a renamed skill; never guess a replacement by display name. Two campaign/hero records remain isolated. Save/load, pack upgrade/downgrade, removed dependencies and missing assets are tested using copies, including active Foot/Mounted presets and shared cooldown groups. Runtime handles/extension instances never enter saves.

## Authoring kit and acceptance

Ship tools/Combat.Authoring with proposed new-pack, add-ability, validate and package operations, schema/editor completion files, commented templates, SDK API reference, troubleshooting and a step-by-step original-animation recipe. Tool operations are template-driven and non-destructive: defaults create new module output, existing files require an explicit replace flag, and validation does not rewrite author content. Validation separates static success from required in-game proof and names missing native tools/build/runtime assumptions. Error fixtures cover ID collisions, missing dependencies, bad ranges, invalid action/category/asset names, context restrictions and effect-provider version mismatch. Packaging verifies required files/dependencies/notices without including proprietary game binaries or another mod's assets.

Include three complete distributable sample modules: a declarative native-animation skill, a pack with original custom foot/mounted combat animation assets and bindings, and an optional C# effect-provider example. Include source files/license/provenance for the original sample art so an author can learn and replace it. Samples are real consumers of the public packaged SDK, not privileged branches compiled into the core solution. Samples may use existing game assets by native reference where permitted; they may not redistribute those assets as original work.

EX06 is the concrete usability gate: an independent author (a fresh worker with no core implementation context is sufficient) receives only the candidate public release, authoring kit and documented prerequisites, then creates a NEW separate ability pack under a fresh namespace. They must alter behavior, add their own compatible original animation, and run one foot and one mounted ability through the real controller loadout/HUD/gameplay/save flow without editing/recompiling the framework or receiving undocumented help. Copying a bundled sample and pressing Play alone is not enough. Record the steps, elapsed asset-creation time separately from onboarding/integration time, tool output, support requests and confusing points; fix tooling/docs and rerun affected steps. No arbitrary promised minute limit or required external human appointment is introduced. Verify the optional provider example builds against the public SDK, and two independently named packs coexist, migrate and survive a missing-pack/reinstall test. The final accepted package hash must include the tested kit/docs; fixes invalidate and refresh affected package/evidence. This extends, rather than replaces, the original controller/combat acceptance.
